SYM key shortcuts require a keyboard that exposes SYM as a modifier to Android. They cannot currently work with keyboards whose firmware converts SYM combinations into final characters or navigation events before PhysiBoard receives them. This includes the Clicks Power Keyboard’s current SYM behaviour.

Fn Layer turns letter keys into navigation and shortcut keys. The result can differ by app because some apps understand Android editor actions, while others only react to real Ctrl shortcuts.
Ctrl-hold navigation When Ctrl-hold navigation is off, physically held Ctrl is passed to the app whenever possible. Shortcuts such as Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, or Ctrl+Z can then work directly in editors.
When Ctrl-hold navigation is on, physically held Ctrl first uses the Fn Layer mappings below. A mapped key performs its configured Fn Layer command.
Double-tap Ctrl Double-tapping Ctrl latches Fn Layer. After that, pressing a letter triggers the Fn Layer mapping until Fn Layer is left again. This is useful for arrows, Page Up/Down, Escape, Tab, and selection commands without holding Ctrl.
Action vs. Native Ctrl Actions such as Copy, Paste, Cut, Select All, and Undo are sent as Android editor actions. They work in many text fields, but not every app supports every action.
Use Native Ctrl when an app expects a real shortcut. For example, mapping I to Native Ctrl sends Ctrl+I, so editors such as Google Docs can use it for italic text. Undo can also be mapped as Native Ctrl if an app handles Ctrl+Z better than Android Undo.
QWERTZ on physical QWERTY Fn Layer uses the physical key position so navigation remains stable. Layout hints on keys show when the active text layout would treat that physical key as a different letter, such as Y/Z on QWERTZ.
Layout-aware app Ctrl shortcuts When held Ctrl is passed to apps, this optional setting can translate Ctrl+letter through the active PhysiBoard layout first. It affects app shortcuts, not the physical Fn Layer grid.
Overrides Each key can be configured as Keycode, Action, Native Ctrl, or None. Use overrides to solve app-specific conflicts without changing the whole mode.
When held Ctrl is passed to apps, translate Ctrl+letter through the active PhysiBoard layout first.

There are two paths for held Ctrl. If Ctrl-hold navigation is on, PhysiBoard handles Ctrl+key with the Fn Layer mappings shown below. If Ctrl-hold navigation is off, PhysiBoard passes Ctrl+key to the app. This option only affects that app path: when enabled, Ctrl+letter is translated through the active PhysiBoard layout first, so shortcuts can follow the letters you type. When disabled, apps receive the original physical key positions.
Use PhysiBoard overrides for selected messaging apps. Tested apps show the strategy PhysiBoard actually uses.

Welcome to PhysiBoard
PhysiBoard is an advanced input method for PKB Android devices with support for Fn Layer, shortcuts, custom keyboard mappings, and more.
Enable PhysiBoard
To get started, you need to enable PhysiBoard as an input method in Android Settings. Tap the button below to open settings.
Select PhysiBoard
To use PhysiBoard, select it among the input methods. The next step lets you choose whether PhysiBoard should use a virtual keyboard or hardware-keyboard mode.
Pick the keyboard surface PhysiBoard should use here.
Titan 2 devices can show an extra IME caption bar under PhysiBoard. This OEM setting hides it and keeps PhysiBoard compact.
After: compact PhysiBoard

To get the most out of PhysiBoard, set the Fn key to act as Ctrl from Android system settings. PhysiBoard can show modifier state in the bottom strip, menu bar, or PhysiBoard statusbar: active one-shot states use the active color, locked states use the locked color.
Mappings can also handle app shortcuts, media controls, Escape, Tab, Page Up/Down, and PhysiBar.

PhysiBoard offers many customization options:
• Customizable keyboard layouts
• Launcher shortcuts & Power Shortcuts
• IME bar can act as a swipe bar to move the cursor
• Custom mappings for Fn Layer
Explore the settings to find the perfect configuration for you!

This feature requires Shizuku to access trackpad events.

1. Install Shizuku from GitHub releases
2. Enable developer options in Android settings
3. Plug your device into a PC with ADB installed
4. Run the command that Shizuku shows in its app
5. Grant permission to PhysiBoard in Shizuku

The feature will work automatically once Shizuku is running.
